title: European Film Academy To Honor Beki Probst, Marin Karmitz & Sandra den Hamer With New Community Award
full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie European Film Academy To Honor Beki Probst, Marin Karmitz & Sandra den Hamer With New Community Award Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea Fund Gets Behind Projects From Tarzan & Arab Nasser, Sofia Alaoui & Amanda Nell Eu Lauren Cohan & Jake Epstein To Co-Star In Eric Stoltz-Directed Rom-Com ‘Both Sides Now’ View All September 30, 2026 3:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Beki Probst, Marin Karmitz, Sandra den Hamer Getty Images The European Film Academy has named Beki Probst , Marin Karmitz and Sandra den Hamer as the first recipients of its new Community Award for an Outstanding Contribution to European Film Culture. The award, paying tribute to “a decisive and continuous contribution over many years to the development and expansion of European film culture”, will be presented during the European Film Awards weekend in Athens in January 2027. The trio will be presented with the award on January 15, on the eve of the main ceremony at the traditional Welcome Night gala dinner, taking place this edition at the Acropolis Museum housing some 4,000 artefacts dating as far back as 1,200 BCE. Related Stories News Netflix Renews Indian Reality Breakout 'Lock Upp' For Second Season News 'Doctor Who': Multiple BBC Studios Labels Likely To Apply For Tender Probst is best known internationally as the founder of the Berlinale’s European Film Market, having entered the cinema world as the founder with her Swiss husband of the Queenie Cinemas in Berne in the 1960s, which grew into a successful chain of arthouse cinemas still existing today. Watch on Deadline Born into a Sephardic Jewish family in Istanbul, Probst studied Law and Journalism and worked briefly as a film journalist. From 1981 to 1988, she was the Berlinale delegate for Turkey and Greece and after initiating Locarno’s industry program, she was asked by Berlinale Director Moritz de Hadeln to start the European Film Market in 1988 in its current form. Under her management, which continued into 2014, the EFM became one of the largest and most important international film market in Europe. She has previously been feted with the Berlinale Camera, the Prix du cinéma Suisse , the French Chevalier des Arts et des Lettres and the Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany. Karmitz is known as the founder of France’s independent exhibitor, producer, film financier and sales agent mk2 film. Born in Romania in 1938, Karmitz arrived in France as a refugee with his family in 1947. After studies at the IDHEC film school in Paris, he worked as assistant director to the filmmakers Jean-Luc Godard, Agnès Varda, Jacques Rozier, Yannick Bellon and Pierre Kast. before directing his first short film, Nuit Noir, Calcutta, based on a screenplay by Marguerite Duras, in 1964. In 1965, he worked with Samuel Beckett on the adaptation of Comédie . In the same year, the feature was selected to open the Venice International Film Festival and shocked audiences with its avant-garde material. He launched mk2 Productions in 1967 and made his feature-length directorial debut with Seven Days Somewhere Else (1968), followed by Comrades (1970) and Blow for Blow (1972), which were screened at international festivals. He opened his first cinema in Paris in 1974 in response to Blow for Blow , about a group of textiles workers who take their factory boss hostage in protest at the work conditions, being shut out of mainstream circuits. In 40 years, he would produce 108 films and distribute over 350 in theatres, among them Krzysztof Kieslowski’s Three Colours trilogy, for which he received a nomination for the European Film Awards 1994, twelve films by Claude Chabrol, Alain Resnais, Louis Malle, the Taviani brothers, Theo Angelopoulos, Lucian Pintilié, Gus Van Sant, Ken Loach, Abbas Kiarostami, Hong Sang-Soo, Michael Haneke, Walter Salles and Xavier Dolan. Den Hamer has an extensive track record in the Dutch film industry. From 2007 to 2023, she was the director of the Netherlands Filmmuseum in Amsterdam. Under her leadership, the re-named Eye Filmmuseum opened a brand-new museum building and a new collection centre in Amsterdam. Its eclectic programming includes large retrospectives, international conferences and as well as exhibitions, exploring the work and careers of filmmakers such as Bela Tarr, Apichatpong Weerasethakul and Alex van Warmerdam among many others. Before that, Sandra den Hamer worked for 23 years at the International Film Festival Rotterdam, including roles as co-ordinator of CineMart and the Hubert Bals Fund. From 1996 to 2007, she directed the festival. She also served as President of the Board of the Association of European Cinematheques (A.C.E.). From 2023 to 2026. she was appointed interim executive director at the Netherlands Film Fund. Today she chairs the Board of the IDFA Institute and the Gerrit Rietveld Academy in Amsterdam. Gathering 5,700 members from more than 50 countries across Europe, the European Film Academy oversees the annual European Film Awards, which alternates taking place in its home city of Berlin and another European city, which is Athens this year. The 39th ceremony marks the second time it is unfolding in its new January slot, after the academy decided to shift it from a long-running December slot to integrate the awards more fully into the wider awards season. title: Hearst Networks UK Buys ‘American Chopper’ Revival Series ‘Orange County Choppers Original’
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Fremantle International Commercial Strategy VP Jill Kellie Exits After Four Years ‘Joseph’s Machines’, ‘Triple Charm’ & ‘What’s Up Moms’ Among Volt Factor Shows Rolling Out On Future Today Channels Hearst Networks UK Buys ‘American Chopper’ Revival Series ‘Orange County Choppers Original’ View All September 30, 2026 3:11am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Orange County Choppers' EXCLUSIVE: Orange County Choppers Originals is headed out of the garage and travelling to Europe. Hearst Networks has bought UK rights to the ‘reborn’ ob doc series from Off The Fence , which has boarded the show after striking an agreement to represent it worldwide (excluding the U.S.). The new series – which aired in the U.S. on Discovery Channel, Discovery Turbo TV, Discovery+, and Discovery GO after launching in February – is the latest chapter in the motorbikes franchise that began in 2002 with American Chopper and is bases around the Orange County Choppers custom bikes business. A second season has been ordered, with the number of eps doubling to 12. Related Stories News Dori Media Hitting Cannes With Unscripted Shows Like 'You Show Know' & 'New Love' Executives V10 Entertainment Gears Up For MIPCOM By Tieing With Former Paramount, Amazon MGM Studios & Vision Plus Execs Prior to Orange County Choppers Originals ‘ launch, there had been no new American Chopper episodes since 2020’s finale, American Chopper: The Last Ride . At one point, there had been a six-year gap due to legal problems between Paul Teutul Sr. and his son, Paul Teutul Jr., the father and son at the center of the series, but they were ultimately settled and the pair reunited on-screen. Watch on Deadline The Hearst agreement, brokered by OTF’s SVP North America and Global Networks, Sam Thompson and Hearst Networks’ Acquisitions Manager, Hannah Gray, marks a first international deal for the revival. Orange County Choppers Originals is based around Teutul Sr., founder and CEO of Orange County Choppers, who has spent over 30 years crafting custom motorcycles for major corporations and sports teams. The series shifts the focus to his workshop in Florida, where he reunites with some of the original team while introducing fresh talent. It also delves into his personal life, highlighting his charity work and passion for animal welfare and rescue on his hobby farm. Hearst’s Gray said: “ Orange County Choppers has everything we look for in great factual entertainment: big builds, strong characters and plenty of heart. With Paul Sr. back at the centre of the story, we’re excited to bring this new chapter to UK audiences.” Orange County Choppers Original sees Teutul Sr.’s team design and build one-of-a-kind motorcycles for charitable causes, with each episode following them through engineering challenges, tight deadlines, and unexpected setbacks, culminating in auctions or raffles to raise funds and awareness. Joan Kay, co-CEO of OCC said: “Everyone loves a comeback story and this one comes with the rebirth of an iconic brand and frankly, Paul Sr. is kicking ass. We’re very excited to partner with OTF on the global revival of the show as the company shares our values of working with entertainment with purpose and has an enviable reach and network of partners around the world across all platforms. “This show isn’t just television, it has proved itself as a cultural phenomenon with the power to ignite fans and enthusiasts and turbocharge bike culture – we can’t wait for you all to see it.” OTF’s Thompson said: “We’ve seized this opportunity wholeheartedly because the facts speak for themselves. There’s an existing fanbase hungry for more, with proven ratings, engagement, sponsorship and merchandising potential. We’re especially excited to have Hearst Networks on board as a quality broadcast partner and look forward to sharing the rollout of this rare gem.” The American Chopper franchise has previously broadcasted in 160 territories in 35 languages worldwide, and OTF’s acquisition offers a new opportunity for buyers at MIPCOM in just under two weeks’ time in Cannes, France. title: London Film Festival: Sam Pollard To Lead Official Competition Jury
full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Ascent Creatives International Launches After DDA Talent & Worldwide Production Merger AI Short Film ‘The Gifted’ Wins Inaugural Future Vision XPRIZE Backed By Range Media Partners & Google SXSW Teen Comedy ‘Edie Arnold Is A Loser’ Lands International Sales Rep View All September 30, 2026 4:29am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Sam Pollard Dia Dipasupil/Getty Images for Tribeca Festival. Legendary documentary filmmaker Sam Pollard will lead the Official Competition jury at this year’s London Film Festival . Pollard will be joined by Argentine filmmaker and writer Mariano Llinás ( The Life of Jorge Luis Borges ) and Julie La Bassiere, Chief Strategy Officer at DDA Global. The ten films in Competition at LFF this year are: • 7 Miles Out — Carol Morley • Act 3 — Christine Molloy and Joe Lawlor • Glaxo — Benjamín Naishtat Related Stories News Paul Thomas Anderson's Cameron Winter Concert Film Joins London Film Festival Lineup As Mubi Acquires World Rights News London Film Festival Lineup: Ava DuVernay's '14th' & Boots Riley's 'I Love Boosters' Among Headline Titles -- Full List • Imperium — Sergei Loznitsa Watch on Deadline • Ketticè — Giovanni Tortorici • Look Back — Hirokazu Koreeda • My Notes on Mars — Lili Horvát • The Difficult Bride — Rubaiyat Hossain • The Idiot(s) — Małgorzata Szumowska and Michal Englert • Woman Unknown — May el-Toukhy The First Feature Competition (Sutherland Award) jury will be led by British Egyptian actor and producer Amir El-Masry. El-Masry won a Scottish BAFTA for his performance in Limbo and was named a 2020 BAFTA Breakthrough Brit. His recent screen work includes the Naseem Hamed biopic Giant and 100 Nights of Hero . Sandhya Suri will lead the Documentary Competition jury. Suri’s Hindi-language narrative fiction debut, Santosh , premiered at Cannes in 2024, won the BIFA for Best Screenplay, was nominated for an Outstanding British Debut BAFTA, and was shortlisted for the Oscars. Suri, who originally made her debut with the 2005 documentary I For India , is now working with BBC Film on a JG Ballard adaptation. T The Short Film Competition jury is led by producer, writer and Erebus Pictures co-founder Helen Simmons. Her producing credits include the BAFTA-nominated Hoard , the 2025 LFF Closing Gala film 100 Nights of Hero , and Berlinale Crystal Bear winner Last Swim . She also co-wrote and co-directed the Méliès Award-winning short Measure . The 2026 London Film Festival runs from October 7 to October 18.
